stem: Which additional history point would most strongly support IgA vasculitis nephritis in a child with haematuria and oedema after a recent sore throat?

options.text: A previous episode of a rash with swollen joints
Fever for 24 hours at the time of presentation
One day of reduced oral intake

explanation: IgA vasculitis nephritis is suggested by a history of a previous rash with swollen joints. This extra-renal clue broadens the differential beyond post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 73

rationale: IgA vasculitis commonly has extra-renal features such as rash and arthralgia. A previous episode of rash with swollen joints supports a vasculitic cause of nephritis.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a prior rash with swollen joints suggests IgA vasculitis, which can be associated with nephritis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because fever is non-specific and does not particularly support IgA vasculitis nephritis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because reduced oral intake is non-specific and does not indicate a vasculitic cause of nephritis.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a family history of hypertension does not help distinguish IgA vasculitis nephritis from other causes.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because dark urine reflects haematuria but does not provide the extra-renal history that suggests IgA vasculitis.
